findings.reason: the measure must be broadened to cover `select(`/`find(` heading lookups (or the enumerator's rewrite of `_authored_section_headings` made the assertion), else the consolidation completes with a second walker and the section's own "underscored at every review" defect recurs.
findings.text: the instrument the done-when runs, as the section specifies it (`find_all` with a heading-tag argument, a `<h2` regex, `_H2_OPEN_RE`, under `reckon/`), cannot see `soup.select("h2[id], section[id]")`, the heading walk inside `_authored_section_headings` that the section names as one to consolidate; the same clause set instead newly reports `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:334` (`find_all(re.compile(r"^h[1-6]$"))`), a walker the section never mentions — so the done-when "runs the instrument at the head and requires it to report only the owner" can pass green with `_authored_section_headings`'s walk surviving, and the stated count of nine places is not what the stated clauses produce (they report thirteen sites across eight files, mcp_views absent, dispatch.py present)

findings.reason: extend `_authored_prose`/`_AuthoredProseParser` to yield per-section prose (it already walks the boundaries) so one owner computes a section's authored content, instead of pairing the span enumerator's offsets with the prose parser's rules.
findings.text: the per-section digest is stated to read the span enumerator for a section's extent while applying "the same prose rules and the same landed-card exclusion", but those rules live in `_authored_prose`/`_AuthoredProseParser` (plan_review.py:257, class at :162), which already tracks section and landed-card boundaries via `_section_is_card`, `_card_depth` and `_heading_depth`; the document unit ("everything authored outside any section") must also know section boundaries, so this parser would have to learn them independently of the enumerator — two owners of "a section's authored content" whose notions of a section must agree before a digest is stable; the owner to extend is `_AuthoredProseParser`, not a second reconciliation of two parsers

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the design consolidates nine heading walkers behind one raw-text enumerator whose interface is identity, heading text and replaced span, which is a smaller interface than the behaviour it hides.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the per-section authored content would be computed from two owners that each track section boundaries rather than one.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1475, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 names its one added public definition (the coverage predicate) and states in its own text why nothing is retired, and reuses the existing plan-review-missing family so no refusal family is added.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites the owners it extends (`_StructuredSectionSpanParser`, `_section_heading`/`_section_body_end`, `_authored_section_headings`, `plan_fingerprint`/`_authored_prose`, `_fingerprint_forms`), but the search instrument it makes the done-when run cannot see one of the walkers it names, and newly reports one it does not.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no thin layer is added; §16 states it extends the prose-digest owner rather than adding a second walker, and extends `_section_heading`/`_section_body_end` rather than forking the collapse span.
